title: Control the process
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which part of your process do you hand to someone else, and what does it cost you?
Jose said the person in the book kept tight control of the manufacturing process, even when many companies sent their factories abroad. That is quality control.

He told of a friend, a partner and mentor, who had a fishing-reel business. A well-known reel maker moved all its manufacturing abroad, and the friend said: the reels will never be the same, so get all the old ones you can. The quality control wasn't there, Jose said, and a competitor took the market.
A student said the person in the book and a famous founder of a computer company differ: one had little interest in manufacturing, the other cared about it more than the product.

groups.heading: A closed system, and the factory as the product

lines.text: Jose said the famous founder criticized the software-only company because anyone could install its software on thousands of computers, whose hardware could be terrible. I believe in a closed system, he said: nobody can install software on my computer, and I have a tight control over the end result and the user interface.

The person in the book takes it another step: not only a closed system, but I'm going to design the factory that makes the products. He said the brain strain of designing the car is tiny compared to designing the factory.

He leaves no room for error, Jose said. He has ultimate control of all the process. I have never seen an entrepreneur with this level of control. A student added: engineering and the design team are one, and so are design and manufacturing.
Where do you want to keep control, and where can you let go?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the parts of your process that decide quality.
Write which of them you control and which you hand off.
Write what happened last time you handed one off.
Write what a closed system would mean for you.
Write the process behind your product, not only the product.

check.q: What did Jose say the person kept control of?
What did Jose say happened to the reel maker's quality after it moved?
What did Jose say is tiny compared to designing the factory?

recap: Control the process that decides your quality. Design the factory, not only the product.
